claims.text: High fractions of light elements such as Al and Ti can give lightweight HEAs low density.
Lightweight HEAs containing Al and Ti can retain high mechanical strength.
Lightweight HEAs containing Al and Ti can exhibit corrosion resistance.
Lightweight HEAs containing light elements can exhibit high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A single lightweight-HEA design can combine low density, strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance because of pronounced lattice distortion.
A baseline alloy with less Al and Ti will generally have less lattice distortion.
A baseline alloy with less Al and Ti will generally have a less uniform microstructure.
Increasing Al and Ti concentrations induces greater lattice distortion.
Rapid solidification or sputtering favors amorphous or nanocrystalline lightweight-HEA microstructures.
A homogeneous amorphous or nanocrystalline matrix with substantial lattice distortion facilitates formation of a continuous protective oxide or passive film.
Lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion and thereby enhances strength.
Lattice distortion encourages uniform Al2O3, Cr2O3, or mixed-oxide scales that improve corrosion and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The high-light-element alloy will have higher yield strength than a lower-light-element baseline.
The high-light-element alloy will have lower corrosion current density than a lower-light-element baseline.
The high-light-element alloy will show less oxidation mass gain than the baseline during exposure near 900 °C.
The modified alloy will maintain a lower density than the baseline.
Excess light-element content that causes phase separation or brittle intermetallic formation will diminish mechanical, corrosion, and oxidation performance.
The proposed comparison should include oxidation near 900 °C, corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl, and mechanical loading.
A high-Al/Ti sample and a lower-Al/Ti control should be prepared under identical processing and compared using structural, mechanical, electrochemical, and oxidation measurements.

The hypothesis is falsified if the modified sample lacks statistically significant improvements in yield strength, oxidation mass gain, and corrosion current density, or develops a discontinuous or nonprotective film.
